rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; project retained. The second applies the Caution's person test (born after January 1, 2008, claimed as a dependent, or a student) to the column's contributions on lines 1 and 2; the project figures lines 1 to 5 as printed and zeroes the ineligible person's column on line 6 (f8880.line6a/6b through f8880.elig_a/elig_b, the same test: person.sav_ineligible is sav_born false, sav_student true, or sa.dependent and sav_claimed both true). Line 7 and every line after it are the same on both sides; only lines 3 and 5 of an ineligible column differ, and the form prints no instruction for where the zero goes. The binding reading amb.2025.savers_ineligible_column (owner decision 4) puts it on line 6 of that column. f8880 p. 1, Caution, "The person(s) who made the qualified contribution or elective deferral (a) was born after January 1, 2008; (b) is claimed as a dependent on someone else's 2025 tax return; or (c) was a student".

Ruling: equivalent; project retained. The project writes the form's stops as a guard (f8880.can_take) and enters zero when one applies; each stop already makes the smaller of lines 10 and 11 zero: no contributions or line 7 zero makes line 10 zero, line 8 over savers.agi_limit has rate 0.0 in the table (so line 10 is zero), and Credit Limit Worksheet line 3 floored at zero makes line 11 zero. f8880 p. 1, line 7, "If zero, stop; you can't take this credit"; line 9, "Note: If line 9 is zero, stop"; f8880 p. 2, Credit Limit Worksheet, line 3, "But if zero or less, stop; you can't take the credit".

Ruling: representation; project retained (as the earlier ruling on this line). On a joint return both sides add both spouses' person.sav_prior_joint, so they agree. They differ only on a return that is not joint, where the second adds the taxpayer's person.sav_prior_joint and the project counts nothing for it: that input is for a joint return only (its question begins "On a joint return:"), and on any other return all of the filer's 2023, 2024 and early-2026 distributions go in person.sav_prior_other ("on a return that is not a joint return: all your distributions in 2023 and 2024, and in 2026 before the due date"; f8880.prior_own_a's label, clarified per Stage 15 question 7, says the same), which both sides count in column (a). f8880 p. 2, Line 4, "Enter the total amount of distributions you, and your spouse if filing jointly, received after 2022 and before the due date of your 2025 return"; "include both spouses' amounts in both columns". The 2026 part follows amb.2025.savers_2026_joint. No change to the data.

Ruling: representation; project retained. On a joint return both sides add both spouses' person.sav_prior_joint (the project by a sum over the two person entries, the second by one sum per role), so they agree. They differ only on a return that is not joint, where the second adds the taxpayer's person.sav_prior_joint and the project counts nothing for it: the project asks that input for a joint return only (its question begins "On a joint return:") and on any other return puts all of the filer's 2023, 2024 and early-2026 distributions in person.sav_prior_other ("on a return that is not a joint return: all your distributions in 2023 and 2024, and in 2026 before the due date"), which both sides count in column (a). f8880 p. 2, Line 4, "Enter the total amount of distributions you, and your spouse if filing jointly, received after 2022 and before the due date of your 2025 return"; "If you're filing a joint return, include both spouses' amounts in both columns. Exception. Don't include your spouse's distributions with yours ... if you and your spouse didn't file a joint return for the year the distribution was received". The 2026 part follows amb.2025.savers_2026_joint.

Ruling: equivalent; project retained. Column (b) is zero on both sides unless the return is joint (f8880 p. 2, Column (b), "Complete column (b) only if you're filing a joint return"); inside that branch the project's inner choose on a joint return always takes the sum of both spouses' person.sav_prior_joint, which is the second's term, and both add the spouse's person.sav_prior_other and the 2025 Forms 1099-R. The redundant guard is all that differs. f8880 p. 2, Line 4, "If you're filing a joint return, include both spouses' amounts in both columns". No change to the data.

Ruling: representation; project retained. As line 4(a), inside the joint-return branch both sides share (column (b) is zero otherwise, f8880 p. 2, Column (b), "Complete column (b) only if you're filing a joint return"). On a joint return both sides add both spouses' person.sav_prior_joint (the project by a sum over the two person entries, the second by one sum per role), so they agree. They differ only on a return that is not joint, where the second adds the taxpayer's person.sav_prior_joint and the project counts nothing for it: the project asks that input for a joint return only (its question begins "On a joint return:") and on any other return puts all of the filer's 2023, 2024 and early-2026 distributions in person.sav_prior_other ("on a return that is not a joint return: all your distributions in 2023 and 2024, and in 2026 before the due date"), which both sides count in column (a). f8880 p. 2, Line 4, "Enter the total amount of distributions you, and your spouse if filing jointly, received after 2022 and before the due date of your 2025 return"; "If you're filing a joint return, include both spouses' amounts in both columns. Exception. Don't include your spouse's distributions with yours ... if you and your spouse didn't file a joint return for the year the distribution was received".
